units.text: Is very implementation focused

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.section: PAIN POINTS — WHY THIS? WHY NOW?
units.text: If we want to operate differently, we can't do so in the old structure — there is a traditional hierarchy built into the organization

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer

units.text: HR drove a lot of past policymaking (structure, comp, leadership models)

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: We used to hire program experts with deep knowledge (Academia model)

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: Shifted towards generalists under single purpose, more of a corporate structure — "braided efforts to execute"

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: Happening over the last decade, previous CEO mobilized people around levers of change, but didn't carry that through to the structure

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: The concept of cross-functional ways of working isn't new to us, that's how we operate externally but not how we operate internally

units.text: "Health would show up in New Mexico and Education would show up in NM. So there wasn't a unified GNP foundation to the community there, there were multiple GNP Foundations"

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: "How do we show up to our grantees to drive systemic change?"

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: Thirds — a third are committed to the need for change, a third are willing and open, a third will be resistors — needing a lot of work (some know what the change implies and won't like it)

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: For resistors, this may revoke the social contract that they were brought here to do

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: Some will just lack the capacity and skills to function as part of a multi-disciplinary team

units.text: We are committed to the success of CEO and the organization

units.text: BUT until we know what shifting roles and duties looks like, people won't be aligned

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: Health and Wellness team, and Economic Security team all feed into the school experience

units.speaker: Chief Operating Officer
units.text: May need to bring in specialists and experts as needed — cross-functional teams would need to be empowered to pull in the resources to get it done

units.text: Old paradigm: who has lead accountability for Community team? Regional lead, education expert, specialist in community engagement?

units.text: We used to have teams solely on cities — Community teams used to hire consultants rather than asking their colleagues

units.text: Very time consuming — and even with this we sometimes fail to make and communicate decisions

units.text: Complicated by lack of prioritizing… too many needs, projects, requests

units.text: Willingness to work through an example, people would start to fidget if we don't talk about the implementation

units.text: What are the critical success factors to create culture change? Implementation and launch?

units.text: Mission driven

units.text: How we communicate this — this is so crucial

units.text: Legacy is very important — incl. vision, mission and values

qa.question: Why do grants take so long?
qa.answer: The lines give no single confirmed cause, only interviewees' views. The Project Manager says the Grant Management Department can hold up grantmaking over lobbying, effectiveness or tax questions, and that decisions need a lot of back and forth across many teams. The Head of Org Effectiveness says Grant Services comes in too late with questions and that processes are too convoluted.
